html:
The Karabakh movement was a mass movement in Armenia that began in February 1988, with huge rallies in Yerevan in support of the Armenians of Nagorno Karabakh, who wanted to join their region to Armenia.

Hundreds of thousands gathered on Theatre Square. The Soviet leadership refused, and violence followed, including the pogrom against Armenians in Sumgait in Azerbaijan in February 1988. The Karabakh Committee, a group of intellectuals, led the protests; its members were jailed after the earthquake of December 1988, then released. The movement turned into a drive for independence, and its leader Levon Ter-Petrosyan became Armenia's first president. It led to the Karabakh war and to the independence vote.
sum: The Karabakh movement was a mass movement in Armenia that began in February 1988, with huge rallies in Yerevan in support of the Armenians of Nagorno Karabakh, who wanted to join their region to Armenia.
